headline: Tk 5.38 billion loan fraud: ACC to charge Salman F Rahman, son and 23 others
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission alleges the funds were embezzled from IFIC Bank through Skymark International and subsequently laundered.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) will bring charges against former Beximco Group vice-chairman Salman F Rahman, his son Ahmed Shayan Fazlur Rahman, and 23 others for embezzling over Tk 5.38 billion from IFIC Bank.
The case centers on loans obtained by Skymark International, which the ACC says were approved in three installments without a proper assessment of the company's ability to repay.
Investigators allege that Tk 5.38 billion was withdrawn in cash or via transfers and misappropriated, then laundered to conceal the source and destination of the funds.
The ACC found that the bank failed to conduct basic 'Know Your Customer' (KYC) checks, ignored financial capacity, and never inspected the borrower's business premises or warehouse.
Furthermore, a proposal to take 650 decimals of land as collateral was put on hold and never completed, leaving the loan unsecured.
As of July 23, the outstanding balance on the loan stood at Tk 6.05 billion, including interest and charges, which the commission has labeled a financial loss for the bank.
This case is part of a wider investigation into allegations that Salman and Shayan secured Tk 71.29 billion in loans through 14 'fake and paper' companies from IFIC Bank.
caption:
Tk 5.38 billion embezzled and laundered. The ACC is now moving to charge Salman F Rahman and his son over a massive IFIC Bank loan fraud.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) will bring charges against former Beximco Group vice-chairman Salman F Rahman, his son Ahmed Shayan Fazlur Rahman, and 23 others for embezzling over Tk 5.38 billion from IFIC Bank.

The case centers on loans obtained by Skymark International, which the ACC says were approved in three installments without a proper assessment of the company's ability to repay.

Investigators allege that Tk 5.38 billion was withdrawn in cash or via transfers and misappropriated, then laundered to conceal the source and destination of the funds.

The ACC found that the bank failed to conduct basic 'Know Your Customer' (KYC) checks, ignored financial capacity, and never inspected the borrower's business premises or warehouse.

Furthermore, a proposal to take 650 decimals of land as collateral was put on hold and never completed, leaving the loan unsecured.

As of July 23, the outstanding balance on the loan stood at Tk 6.05 billion, including interest and charges, which the commission has labeled a financial loss for the bank.

This case is part of a wider investigation into allegations that Salman and Shayan secured Tk 71.29 billion in loans through 14 'fake and paper' companies from IFIC Bank.

headline_marked: September deadliest month as [[Dhaka doctor dies of dengue]]
headline: September deadliest month as Dhaka doctor dies of dengue
summary: Anchal Roy, a 30-year-old assistant registrar, passed away while undergoing treatment at Square Hospital amid a sharp rise in cases.
details: Anchal Roy, a 30-year-old assistant registrar at the respiratory medicine department of Mugda Medical College Hospital, has died of dengue.
She passed away while undergoing treatment in the intensive care unit of Square Hospital in Dhaka.
Her death occurs during a period of significant increase in dengue infections and fatalities across the country.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), September has become the deadliest month of this year's outbreak.
DGHS data shows 35,690 cases and 122 deaths were recorded up to September 26.
As of Saturday, a total of 219 people have died of dengue this year, with 71,536 patients hospitalized.
caption:
A 30-year-old doctor dies of dengue as September becomes the deadliest month of the year.

Anchal Roy, a 30-year-old assistant registrar at the respiratory medicine department of Mugda Medical College Hospital, has died of dengue.

She passed away while undergoing treatment in the intensive care unit of Square Hospital in Dhaka.

Her death occurs during a period of significant increase in dengue infections and fatalities across the country.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), September has become the deadliest month of this year's outbreak.

DGHS data shows 35,690 cases and 122 deaths were recorded up to September 26.

As of Saturday, a total of 219 people have died of dengue this year, with 71,536 patients hospitalized.
